overall: Tomorrow in Atlanta looks to be a warm early-June day, with the ensemble model pointing to a high in the mid-80s°F. Conditions appear seasonably warm but there is notable uncertainty in the forecast, with models showing a wide spread rather than a tight consensus. No strong single-scenario signal dominates the outlook.
forecast_obs_notes: Model agreement is poor — GFS is a significant outlier, assigning 34% probability to the 88-89°F bucket while ECMWF, HRRR, NBM, and WEATHER.COM each score only 3-4% for that same bucket. This large divergence, with GFS running much warmer than all other guidance, inflates the top predicted bucket and undermines confidence in any single temperature range.
max_temp_prediction: The ensemble mean TMAX of 84.6°F is the most defensible central estimate, as the 88-89°F top bucket is driven almost entirely by GFS rather than broad model agreement. Today's observed running max of 73.4°F provides limited carry-over context but does not contradict a mid-80s peak tomorrow. Confidence is low given both prediction tiers are rated Tier 4 (Poor signals), and the wide model spread warrants caution on any temperature bet.
